title: As AI eats the web, the internet’s collective memory is disappearing
titleZh: 随着人工智能吞噬网络，互联网的集体记忆正在消失
author: awnird
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: figassis
comments.textRawHtml: I called this maybe 3y ago, but I think so did everyone else that was sane. Sure, we get immense value from AI, but indiscriminately injecting into everything, the one thing we know to be unreliable above the threshold we used to fire people for, is probably the greatest undoing of all the good companies like Google brought to the internet. I mean what a way to destroy your legacy of democratizing information. The amount of harm (direct and indirect) this will cause, and the cost to return to baseline will be so immense, and yet we will not be able to point to the root cause. They won't be there to take responsibility.
comments.textZhHtml: 我大概在 3 年前就这么称呼过，但我想其他理智的人也是这么称呼的。当然，我们从人工智能中获得了巨大的价值，但不加区别地注入一切，我们知道，超过我们用来解雇员工的门槛的一件事是不可靠的，这可能是像谷歌这样进入互联网的所有优秀公司的最大毁灭。我的意思是，这是一种摧毁你们民主化信息遗产的方式。这将造成的伤害（直接和间接）以及恢复基线的成本将是巨大的，但我们无法指出根本原因。他们不会在那里承担责任。

children.author: customguy
children.textRawHtml: I called it 2001/2002 or whenever they appeared when I tried to explain why personalized search results are the beginning of the end of a shared reality and therefore the ability to reason and act in public, and with others. I bet some still consider it hyperbole. It's just taking in trends and seeing where the glacier moves to, how the cookie will crumble so to speak.
children.textZhHtml: 我称其为 2001/2002，或者每当它们出现时，我试图解释为什么个性化搜索结果是共享现实终结的开始，因此是在公共场合以及与他人一起推理和行动的能力。我敢打赌有些人仍然认为这有点夸张。它只是了解趋势，看看冰川移动到哪里，可以这么说，饼干将如何破碎。

children.author: nuclearnicer
children.textRawHtml:
It is an astute point. I agree that we have largely lost a lot of our shared reality. But as with any "beginning" of a long, diffuse process, people might quibble about the specifics.

I offer a few other moments you might gesture toward as the beginning of the end of shared reality.

First, 1987, with the elimination of the Fairness Doctrine and the subsequent boom in partisan talk radio shows.

Second, 1989, when cable TV became a mature technology reaching half of U.S. households.

And finally, maybe a lesser item, the introduction of the DVR circa 2000, when we stopped watching scheduled TV together.

I wonder if more historically informed people would find the fracturing going further back as other advancements in publishing technology allowed more people to share more views.
children.textZhHtml:
这是一个精明的观点。我同意我们在很大程度上失去了很多共同的现实。但就像一个漫长而分散的过程的任何“开始”一样，人们可能会对具体细节争论不休。

我提供了一些你可能会认为是共享现实终结的开始的其他时刻。

首先是 1987 年，随着公平主义的废除以及随后党派谈话广播节目的繁荣。

第二个是 1989 年，当时有线电视成为一项成熟的技术，覆盖了美国一半的人口。最后，也许是一个较小的项目，大约 2000 年 DVR 的引入，当时我们不再一起观看预定的电视节目。

我想知道，随着出版技术的其他进步允许更多的人分享更多的观点，更多了解历史的人是否会发现更早的破裂。

children.author: zajio1am
children.textRawHtml: Well, loss of (control over) shared narrative was one of complains of the Church against the printing press ...
children.textZhHtml: 嗯，失去（控制）共同叙事是教会对印刷机的抱怨之一......

children.author: smegger001
children.textRawHtml:
And institutional control of information didnt really start again until the Statute of Anne struck up a deal between printers and the state giving printers copyright over written works and the state the right to cencor and ban works the disapproved of nearly 250 years latter.

Radio gave us Demagogues like Father Coughlin in the US and Hitler in Germany, and we still havent dealt with the problems radio introduced when television came along and now we have the internet with social media, podcast, and algorithmic echochambers, and algorithm induced radicalization. Radio television internet any one is just as much a shock to society as print was and we still havent figured out how to adapt yet to any fully.
children.textZhHtml:
直到《安妮法》在印刷商和国家之间达成协议，赋予印刷商书面作品的版权，以及国家审查和禁止近 250 年后不被认可的作品的权利，信息的制度控制才真正开始重新开始。

广播给我们带来了像美国的考夫林神父和德国的希特勒这样的煽动者，我们仍然没有处理电视出现时广播带来的问题，现在我们已经互联网与社交媒体、播客和算法回声室，以及算法引发了激进化。广播电视互联网对社会的冲击与印刷品一样大，但我们仍然没有弄清楚如何完全适应任何一种。

children.author: hnlmorg
children.textRawHtml:
What even is a “shared reality”? For example my mum and I could watch the exact same movie and showing at the cinema and still come away with a completely different opinion of it.

And even when TV was limited to a small few national OTA (over the air) channels, different people would tune in at different times to watch their different preference of shows. So just because content was fewer, it didn’t necessarily equate to different people consuming the same content.

The real crux of the modern problem isn’t preference drive choices. It’s independent publishers being driven out by corporate greed. Eg AI traffic making it unviable for independent blogs. But then one could argue that the current ecosystem, where the barrier for publishing being so low, is an anomaly because historically that was always prohibitively expensive. To go back to the TV example: you couldn’t commission a show without deep pockets and a lot of TV exec contacts.

I’d love our golden age of information to be persistent. But, and as yourself and others have alluded to, that’s not guaranteed unless we fight to keep it that way.
children.textZhHtml:
什么是“共享现实”？例如，我和我妈妈可以在电影院观看完全相同的电影和放映，但仍然对它有完全不同的看法。

即使电视仅限于少数几个全国性 OTA（无线）频道，不同的人也会在不同的时间收看他们不同的节目偏好。因此，仅仅因为内容较少，并不一定意味着不同的人消费相同的内容。

现代问题的真正症结不是偏好驱动选择。独立出版商被企业的贪婪驱逐。例如，人工智能流量使得独立博客变得不可行。但人们可能会说，当前的生态系统（出版门槛如此之低）是一种反常现象，因为从历史上看，出版成本总是高得令人望而却步。回到电视的例子：如果没有雄厚的资金和大量的电视高管联系人，你就无法委托制作一档节目。

我希望我们的信息黄金时代能够持续下去。但是，正如您和其他人所提到的，除非我们努力保持这种状态，否则这并不能得到保证。

children.author: switchbak
children.textRawHtml:
I think of it more as a basis for shared culture - I could chat about Seinfeld / Friends, and odds were high that the other person would know what I was talking about.

I imagine in prior ages this was perhaps more about folks reading a core collection of books. I expect there was less shared culture than in ^

Now it seems like we're in an era with (potentially) less of a shared cultural bases than either of those times. I've certainly met people where there's really no overlap - their core beliefs, values, etc - fundamentally different foundations. If that becomes more widespread, it's hard to know what that will do to our societies.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为它更多地是共享文化的基础 - 我可以谈论《宋飞正传》/《老友记》，而其他人知道我在说什么的可能性很高。

我想在以前的时代，这可能更多是关于人们阅读核心书籍集。我预计共享文化比以前要少^

现在看来，我们正处于一个（可能）比以前更少共享文化基础的时代。我确实见过这样的人实际上没有重叠——他们的核心信仰、价值观等——根本不同的基础。如果这种情况变得更加普遍，很难知道这会对我们的社会产生什么影响。

children.author: customguy
children.textRawHtml:
> For example my mum and I could watch the exact same movie and showing at the cinema and still come away with a completely different opinion of it.

yeah because there is a shared reality in which you can both see the same movie. enjoy it while it lasts.
children.textZhHtml:
> 例如，我和我妈妈可以观看完全相同的电影并在电影院放映，但仍然对它有完全不同的看法。

是的，因为存在一个共同的现实，即你们都可以看到同一部电影。趁它持续的时候享受它。

children.author: vlan0
children.textRawHtml:
>What even is a “shared reality”? For example my mum and I could watch the exact same movie and showing at the cinema and still come away with a completely different opinion of it.

Exactly. The shared reality is the experience. You both were given the same opportunity to take in the same information. The different opinion is what comes out of the other side of the meat suit processing the experience.

Algo driven results changes the experience by changing what the user perceives. So there might never be a shared experience.
children.textZhHtml:
>什么是“共享现实”？例如，我和我妈妈可能在电影院观看完全相同的电影并放映，但仍然对它有完全不同的看法。

完全正确。共同的现实就是体验。你们都有相同的机会接受相同的信息。不同的观点来自于处理体验的肉套装的另一面。

算法驱动的结果通过改变用户的感知来改变体验。因此可能永远不会有共同的经历。

children.author: ndriscoll
children.textRawHtml: Independent blogs are perfectly viable. It is basically free to publish. What's not viable and never was is to be a professional blogger. At best, some people could try to be professional shills with blogs as bait (it is good if these go away; they were noise), and an extremely tiny minority might actually make a living with people paying to support their blog directly.
children.textZhHtml: 独立博客是完全可行的。基本上是免费发布的。成为一名专业博主是不可行的，也从来没有可行过。充其量，有些人可以尝试以博客为诱饵，成为专业的托儿（如果这些消失就好了；它们是噪音），而极少数人实际上可能靠直接付费支持他们的博客的人谋生。

children.author: chrisjj
children.textRawHtml:
> What even is a “shared reality”? For example my mum and I could watch the exact same movie and showing at the cinema and still come away with a completely different opinion of it.

A: It excludes opinion.
children.textZhHtml:
> 什么是“共享现实”？例如，我和我妈妈可能在电影院观看完全相同的电影并放映，但仍然对它有完全不同的看法。

答：它排除了意见。

children.author: benfortuna
children.textRawHtml: Everything is opinion. A shared reality is just where opinions coincide.
children.textZhHtml: 一切都是观点。共同的现实就是观点的一致。

children.author: ryandrake
children.textRawHtml:
The shared reality in that example includes only facts: OP and mum went to a movie. The movie was called X. The actors were Y and Z.

The original point of this subthread was that we can't even agree on a shared set of facts anymore! The political Right has an entirely different set of facts than the political Left, and when our reality is derived from those facts, we cannot share the same reality anymore.
children.textZhHtml:
该示例中的共同现实仅包括事实：OP 和妈妈去看了电影。这部电影被称为 X。演员是 Y 和 Z。

这个子线程的初衷是我们甚至不能再就一组共同的事实达成一致！政治右派拥有与政治左派完全不同的事实，当我们的现实源自这些事实时，我们就不能再分享相同的现实了。

children.author: switchbak
children.textRawHtml:
Everything is perceived, and our perception gets filtered based on our prior experience. Just because we're not directly perceiving objective reality, that does not mean _everything_ is opinion.

JFK was shot, that's not just my opinion.

Unless you choose to believe some kind of post-modern crazyness, in which case - have at it.
children.textZhHtml:
一切都是感知的，我们的感知会根据我们之前的经验进行过滤。仅仅因为我们没有直接感知客观现实，并不意味着_一切_都是观点。

肯尼迪被枪杀，这不仅仅是我的观点。

除非你选择相信某种后现代的疯狂，在这种情况下 - 那就去做吧。

children.author: the_af
children.textRawHtml:
Not necessarily. A shared reality is one where people are discussing the same thing (within a reasonable margin) even if filtered by their individual perceptions, and drawing different conclusions.

I don't know the word for the opposite of shared reality (maybe private individualized realities), but it results in a scenario where you have nothing in common with other people other than "I saw some thing" and therefore it becomes very difficult to discuss anything with them.
children.textZhHtml:
不一定。共享现实是指人们在讨论同一件事（在合理的范围内），即使受到个人看法的过滤，并得出不同的结论。

我不知道共享现实的反义词（也许是私人的个性化现实），但它会导致一种情况，除了“我看到了一些东西”之外，你与其他人没有任何共同点，因此与他们讨论任何事情都变得非常困难。

children.author: win311fwg
children.textRawHtml: If everything is opinion then there can be no shared reality. The only "reality" that exists is your opinion about there being one.
children.textZhHtml: 如果一切都是观点，那么就不可能有共同的现实。唯一存在的“现实”是您对存在的看法。

children.author: parineum
children.textRawHtml: Like whether you teo were even in the same room watching that movie.
children.textZhHtml: 就像你们是否在同一个房间看那部电影。

children.author: rayiner
children.textRawHtml: That was a temporary blip. Specific technologies facilitated an age of mass, top-down communications in the mid 20th century, just by virtue of how those technologies worked. It enabled a small group of people in charge of the radio/TV stations to have a monopoly on communications and media. The technology both before (printing presses with myriad newspapers) and after (the Internet) were by their nature decentralized.
children.textZhHtml: 那只是暂时现象。正是由于这些技术的运作方式，特定技术在 20 世纪中叶促进了大规模、自上而下的通信时代。它使一小部分广播电台/电视台的负责人垄断了通讯和媒体。之前的技术（印有无数报纸的印刷机）和之后的技术（互联网）本质上都是去中心化的。

children.author: flir
children.textRawHtml:
Not totally convinced about the printing press example (expensive, technical). The biggest presses, with the longest reach (daily newspapers) were often owned by the richest people.

What's unique now is decentralized + extreme potential reach. Or it was. Now we have to consider bias in the algorithm that sticks stuff in front of us and is, I suspect, the modern equivalent of those daily newspaper presses.
children.textZhHtml:
不完全相信印刷机的例子（昂贵，技术性）。影响范围最广的最大媒体（日报）通常由最富有的人拥有。

现在的独特之处在于去中心化+极大的潜在影响范围。或者说确实如此。现在我们必须考虑算法中的偏见，该算法将东西放在我们面前，我怀疑，它相当于那些日报的现代版本。

children.author: dragontamer
children.textRawHtml:
Rich _people_ yes.

But corporations were an act of Congress in 1776. Early America was decidedly anti-corporate (the Boston Tea Party was about a tax break to a corporation). Early Americans (and early thinkers who influenced Americans) were grossly distrustful of corporations and pools of money.

> The directors with of such [joint-stock] companies, however, being the managers rather of other people's money than of their own, it cannot well be expected, that they should watch over it with the same anxious vigilance with which the partners in a private copartnery frequently watch over their own

Adam Smith, the Wealth of Nations
children.textZhHtml:
富人_是的。

但公司是 1776 年国会的一项法案。早期的美国显然是反公司的（波士顿茶党是关于对公司的税收减免）。早期的美国人（以及影响美国人的早期思想家）对公司和资金池非常不信任。

>然而，这种[股份制]公司的董事是别人的钱而不是他们自己的钱的管理者，所以不能指望他们会像私人合伙人中的合伙人经常监视自己的钱一样焦急地监视着自己的钱。

亚当·斯密，《财富》国家
